findings.body: Live stream receipts remain only in memory until the generation's `done` flush persists them. An allowed member can open a Discord thread on the bot's visible streaming message and send an unmentioned follow-up while the original stream continues. Discord maps that message to a separate thread queue (`channels/discord/conversation-context.ts:324–327`), so the exact-queue check in `live-admission-work-item-repository.postgres.ts:192` does not mark it as received during the running turn. The bot-reference lookup also finds nothing because the visible root has not been persisted, and `group-processing.ts:240–254` consumes the follow-up without running the agent. Slack replies opening a thread on a top-level streaming answer have the same gap. New evidence beyond the receipt/reset rulings: the reply-reference tests finish the stream at `bot-delivery-reply-references.postgres.integration.test.ts:316` before checking replies, so they cannot detect admission while the original stream is still running. Persist acknowledged live references through the existing message projection before another queue evaluates them, and cover a bot-rooted follow-up with the original stream held open.
